assets.name: Arcane Workbench
assets.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: Don't Starve Together in-world building sprite. Three reference images have separate roles: Image 1 is the exact approved geometric edit target from the later v3 set; Image 2 is the earlier v3 version of this same building and supplies its richer main local-color palette and, where wood exists, its preferred wood treatment; Image 3 is the current mod ember lamp and supplies ONLY the rendering language and amount of material detail. Never borrow Image 3's geometry, components, proportions, or empty-lamp/base-edit instructions. Preserve Image 1's silhouette, perspective, proportions, structure, connections, identity symbols, object placement, camera, canvas registration and complete visible footprint. This is a material/color treatment edit, not a redesign.

Target: Arcane Workbench.
Preserve the broad timber tabletop, all four crooked splayed legs and their straps, front drawer and gold ring handle. Preserve the tall cyan crystal in its gold claw-like crown on the round left pedestal; the open ivory book on the right with its existing purple compass/star and crescent/star diagrams, strap, ribbon and fittings; black quill and gold inkpot; bottle and candle; gold bowl containing purple shards and the small papers. Preserve the burgundy cloth over the front-left with its gold compass emblem, and the dangling purple gem and gold crescent on the right. Retain every attachment, overlap, object count and exact placement.

Restore Image 2's deeper, richer main colors and its local value/saturation relationships on corresponding parts while retaining Image 1's shapes. Do not make the result pale, chalky or washed out; do not apply a blanket saturation filter. Match Image 3's actual visible texture density and hand-painted finish at comparable object display scale: neither busier nor cleaner than the lamp. Reduce scattered fine lines while retaining enough selective material marks to belong to the very same mod building set.

For timber only, use the earlier Image 2 wood treatment: rich brown, several irregular medium-size planes, a few long tapered directional splits and selective edge wear. Keep the natural irregular wood shape. Do not substitute pale, smoothly faceted plastic wood or return to dense hairline grain. The ivory book and paper remain calm, intact light surfaces with their existing diagrams; do not add crumple facets or wood texture to paper. Brass, cloth and crystal retain their own distinct material language.

Highest priority is native DST style, following the corrected lamp appearance prompt: heavy varied outer silhouette, dark wedges at important joints, thinner internal structure, and extremely sparse material marks used only where the lamp uses them. Clean broad color areas with a few shaped, hand-painted hard-edged highlights; stone reads as large muted gray-purple facets and brass as warm muted gold planes. Interpret sparse marks by the actual Image 3 lamp, not by making the buildings cleaner than it. Preserve medium-scale material variation without fine-line clutter. No all-over paper texture, granular weathering, dense hatching across surfaces, glossy 3D rendering, uniform bevels, soft bloom or colored cloud.

Output one single complete building at the same camera angle and registration as Image 1. True transparent RGBA background and true transparent gaps/holes; retain the opaque dark cavity where the building itself requires it. Keep the entire silhouette and feet visible with transparent margin. No baked ground shadow, floor, dirt patch, backdrop, checkerboard, scene, labels, typography, border or comparison layout. Do not alter or remove existing functional components.
